ACCOUNTING SERVICES
PROPOSAL
P R O P O S E D  B Y
THE AUTISM CENTRE OF TORONTO
MAY 2026

CONTEXT & OBJECTIVES
Autism Centre of Toronto provides fee-based therapeutic services
to children and families with autism - including early intervention,
applied behaviour analysis, speech, and occupational therapy. With
an annual operating budget of approximately $1.4M, the
organization has recently achieved charitable status and is actively
growing its grant and donation revenue alongside its core fee
income.
The organization has a solid QBO foundation (clear class structure
across five service programs) and is current on all CRA filings. The
immediate need is to replace the current bookkeeping and payroll
function as administrator prepares to go on maternity leave.
Key Characteristics of This Engagement
~$1.4M annual budget; April–March fiscal year
Revenue mix: ~80% fee-for-service, ~15% grants, ~5% donations
19 employees, primarily full-time; bi-weekly payroll via ADP
Five service programs as QBO classes: Early Intervention,
Developmental Classroom, School Readiness, School Support,
Home-Based Services
Government grant requires monthly allocation across programs
Bi-annual grant reporting; quarterly board financial reporting
Currently HST exempt; PSB rebate eligibility to be explored
This proposal is structured in three parts: 
Part A covers ongoing bookkeeping, payroll, financial management
Part B covers a one-time process and digital transformation
engagement to implement and modernize key workflows
Part C covers a one-time year-end and audit support engagement

PART A - ONGOING SERVICES
1) BOOKKEEPING & RECONCILIATIONS
Invoicing & Accounts Receivable:
Generate and issue monthly fee invoices across service programs
Track outstanding AR and follow up on overdue accounts
Record and reconcile incoming payments against invoices
Work toward automating invoice delivery and payment collection 
Income & Expense Recording:
Record all revenue: fee payments, grant, donations
Allocate  grant revenue across program classes 
Categorize all expenses with proper GL coding by program class
Manage restricted vs. unrestricted fund categorization
Accounts Payable:
Process vendor invoices and employee reimbursements 
Manage twice-monthly payment runs with ED 
Maintain full AP documentation in QBO
Reconciliations:
Monthly bank, credit card, and trial balance reconciliations
Reconcile ADP payroll entries to QBO each pay cycle (and QBO
Payroll post-migration)
QBO Maintenance:
Maintain COA and class structure across all service programs
Configure and maintain budget vs. actuals tracking 
Support annual budget entry at the start of each fiscal year

2. PAYROLL ADMINISTRATION & COMPLIANCE
Bi-weekly payroll management for 19 employees currently processed
through ADP. We will manage payroll within ADP for the next 1-2
months before transitioning to QBO payroll (Part B scope)
Payroll Processing:
Manage bi-weekly payroll cycles for full-time and part-time staff
Process employee changes: new hires, terminations, updates
Ensure employee benefits deductions are maintained in system
Maintain and update employee records in payroll system
CRA Compliance & Remittances:
Ensure accurate CPP, EI, and tax source deductions each cycle
Submit federal and provincial payroll remittances on time
Oversee ADP remittance process and reconcile to QBO
Year-End Payroll Filings:
Prepare and file T4 slips for employees and T4A for contractors
Issue Records of Employment (ROEs) as required
Maintain complete payroll records for audit purposes
PART A - ONGOING SERVICES

3. FINANCIAL REPORTING & COMPLIANCE
Ongoing reporting support for the Executive Director and Board,
plus full compliance management throughout the year.
Monthly & Board Reporting:
Monthly financial statements: P&L (program-level), Balance Sheet,
Cash Flow, AR/AP Aging
Monthly budget vs. actuals for ED review
Quarterly board reporting package: Balance Sheet, Statement of
Operations, budget vs. actuals with commentary
Annual General Meeting (AGM) financial package
Help pull any financial inputs for bi-annual government grant
report (submission will be compiled by ED)
HST & PSB Rebate:
Confirm HST-exempt status and assess PSB (Public Service
Bodies) rebate eligibility - TACT may be eligible to reclaim a
portion of HST paid on purchases as a registered charity
File HST returns and manage PSB rebate claims once confirmed
CRA & Audit Compliance:
Liaise with auditor for yearly audit; starting fiscal 2026-2027
Ensure ongoing CRA compliance for registered charities
throughout the year
Support T3010 Registered Charity Information Return (typically
filed by the auditor - we will coordinate and provide financial
inputs)
PART A - ONGOING SERVICES

PART B - PROCESS TRANSFORMATION 
(ONE-TIME ENGAGEMENT)
Following onboarding and an initial stabilization period, we
recommend a targeted digital transformation engagement to
modernize three key workflows. This is scoped as a one-time
project, delivered over approximately 8–10 weeks.
Initiative 1: Accounts Payable Automation via Plooto
Full setup and integration of Plooto with QBO
Configure approval workflows so all payables are routed to the
ED for one-click approval - no direct bank access required
Set up bi-monthly AP payment aligned to bookkeeping cadence
Replace the current manual OneDrive-based expense
reimbursement tracking with a Plooto expense submission form
Staff onboarding and support through the first 2 payment cycles
Initiative 2: Payroll Migration - ADP to QBO Payroll
Migrate all 19 employees from ADP to QuickBooks Online Payroll
Transfer YTD payroll balance, employee record, deductions
Set up benefits deductions: medical, dental, LTD, AD&D in QBO
Configure direct integration between QBO Payroll and ledger
Parallel run for one pay cycle to validate accuracy before cutoff
Staff training and documentation
Initiative 3: Invoicing & AR Automation
Assess current invoicing setup and identify feasilble tools
Build standardized invoice templates for each service program
Set up recurring monthly invoices where applicable
Configure pre-authorized debit (PAD) or automated payment
collection where families consent
Set up automated invoice and payment reminder emails
Establish a clear AR follow-up workflow for outstanding balances

PART C - YEAR-END AUDIT SUPPORT 
(ANNUAL ENGAGEMENT)
Year-end and audit support for the 2025–2026 fiscal year is scoped
as a standalone one-time engagement, independent of the ongoing
monthly retainer, and includes a full review of the year's books,
outstanding reconciliations, and audit preparation.
Step 1: Year-End Book Review & Clean-Up
Conduct a deep review of the full fiscal year (April–March) 
Identify and resolve any adjustments, reclassifications, accruals,
or outstanding reconciling items
Ensure all revenue streams (fees, grants, donations) are
properly recorded and coded by program class
Validate deferred revenue, prepaid expenses, and any balance
sheet items requiring adjustment
Reconcile ADP payroll records to QBO for the full fiscal year
Step 2: Audit Preparation & Working Papers
Prepare year-end financial statementsand all audit schedules,
reconciliations, and supporting documentation
Build the PBC (Prepared By Client) list and ensure items are
complete before the auditor starts
Coordinate year-end documents from the ED: board minutes,
grant agreements, signed contracts
Step 3: Auditor Liaison & Audit Management
Serve as the primary point of contact with the auditor 
Respond to auditor queries and information requests in 2 days
Attend auditor meetings and manage all follow-up items
Implement any post-audit adjustments and journal entries
recommended by the auditor

PROPOSED FEES
PART A - MONTHLY ONGOING RETAINER
Service Module Fee (per month)
1.Bookkeeping & Reconciliations $1,250
2.Payroll Administration & Compliance $1,000
3.Financial Reporting & Year End Compliance (included)
TOTAL $2,250 

PART B - PROCESS & DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION (ONE-TIME)
Service Module Fee (one-time)
1.Accounts Payable Automation via Plooto $2,000
2.Payroll Migration — ADP to QBO Payroll $3,500
3.Invoicing & AR Automation $1,800
TOTAL $7,300

PART C - AUDIT SUPPORT (ANNUAL)
Service Module Fee (annual)
Year end audit support including reasonable
clean up, audit prep and liaison with auditors* $3,500
TOTAL $3,500

*Based on our initial review, some clean-up and reconciliation work will be required. Final fee
will be confirmed once we have completed a full assessment of the books.
Note: Each initiative can be phased and contracted independently, allowing TACT to prioritize
and implement changes at a pace that works for the organization.
Note: Does not include software subscription fees (QBO, Plooto, etc).

WHY US?
Sympl Solutions is committed to ensuring a high standard of financial
clarity and timely support. We bring:
A responsive, detail-oriented team
Decade-long expertise in nonprofit and charity finance
Streamlined tech integration and clear process flows
BIPOC and immigrant-led leadership with lived experiences in
community, social service and arts & culture
We value thoughtful system design, clarity in reporting, and
building long-term trusted partnerships
Any new requirements or adjustments can be discussed and
integrated as needed. We work with transparency, flexibility, and a
commitment to helping our partners thrive.

ACCOUNTING SERVICES PROPOSAL

PROPOSED BY

THE AUTISM CENTRE OF TORONTO

MAY 2026

CONTEXT & OBJECTIVES
Autism Centre of Toronto provides fee-based therapeutic services to children and families with autism - including early intervention, applied behaviour analysis, speech, and occupational therapy. With an annual operating budget of approximately $1.4M, the organization has recently achieved charitable status and is actively growing its grant and donation revenue alongside its core fee income.
The organization has a solid QBO foundation (clear class structure across five service programs) and is current on all CRA filings. The immediate need is to replace the current bookkeeping and payroll function as administrator prepares to go on maternity leave.

Key Characteristics of This Engagement
• ~$1.4M annual budget; April–March fiscal year
• Revenue mix: ~80% fee-for-service, ~15% grants, ~5% donations
• 19 employees, primarily full-time; bi-weekly payroll via ADP
• Five service programs as QBO classes: Early Intervention, Developmental Classroom, School Readiness, School Support, Home-Based Services
• Government grant requires monthly allocation across programs
• Bi-annual grant reporting; quarterly board financial reporting
• Currently HST exempt; PSB rebate eligibility to be explored

This proposal is structured in three parts:
• Part A covers ongoing bookkeeping, payroll, financial management
• Part B covers a one-time process and digital transformation engagement to implement and modernize key workflows
• Part C covers a one-time year-end and audit support engagement

PART A - ONGOING SERVICES
1) BOOKKEEPING & RECONCILIATIONS
Invoicing & Accounts Receivable:
• Generate and issue monthly fee invoices across service programs
• Track outstanding AR and follow up on overdue accounts
• Record and reconcile incoming payments against invoices
• Work toward automating invoice delivery and payment collection

Income & Expense Recording:
• Record all revenue: fee payments, grant, donations
• Allocate grant revenue across program classes
• Categorize all expenses with proper GL coding by program class
• Manage restricted vs. unrestricted fund categorization

Accounts Payable:
• Process vendor invoices and employee reimbursements
• Manage twice-monthly payment runs with ED
• Maintain full AP documentation in QBO

Reconciliations:
• Monthly bank, credit card, and trial balance reconciliations
• Reconcile ADP payroll entries to QBO each pay cycle (and QBO Payroll post-migration)

QBO Maintenance:
• Maintain COA and class structure across all service programs
• Configure and maintain budget vs. actuals tracking
• Support annual budget entry at the start of each fiscal year

2. PAYROLL ADMINISTRATION & COMPLIANCE
Bi-weekly payroll management for 19 employees currently processed through ADP. We will manage payroll within ADP for the next 1-2 months before transitioning to QBO payroll (Part B scope).

Payroll Processing:
• Manage bi-weekly payroll cycles for full-time and part-time staff
• Process employee changes: new hires, terminations, updates
• Ensure employee benefits deductions are maintained in system
• Maintain and update employee records in payroll system

CRA Compliance & Remittances:
• Ensure accurate CPP, EI, and tax source deductions each cycle
• Submit federal and provincial payroll remittances on time
• Oversee ADP remittance process and reconcile to QBO

Year-End Payroll Filings:
• Prepare and file T4 slips for employees and T4A for contractors
• Issue Records of Employment (ROEs) as required
• Maintain complete payroll records for audit purposes

3. FINANCIAL REPORTING & COMPLIANCE
Ongoing reporting support for the Executive Director and Board, plus full compliance management throughout the year.

Monthly & Board Reporting:
• Monthly financial statements: P&L (program-level), Balance Sheet, Cash Flow, AR/AP Aging
• Monthly budget vs. actuals for ED review
• Quarterly board reporting package: Balance Sheet, Statement of Operations, budget vs. actuals with commentary
• Annual General Meeting (AGM) financial package
• Help pull any financial inputs for bi-annual government grant report (submission will be compiled by ED)

HST & PSB Rebate:
• Confirm HST-exempt status and assess PSB (Public Service Bodies) rebate eligibility - TACT may be eligible to reclaim a portion of HST paid on purchases as a registered charity
• File HST returns and manage PSB rebate claims once confirmed

CRA & Audit Compliance:
• Liaise with auditor for yearly audit; starting fiscal 2026-2027
• Ensure ongoing CRA compliance for registered charities throughout the year
• Support T3010 Registered Charity Information Return (typically filed by the auditor - we will coordinate and provide financial inputs)

PART B - PROCESS TRANSFORMATION (ONE-TIME ENGAGEMENT)
Following onboarding and an initial stabilization period, we recommend a targeted digital transformation engagement to modernize three key workflows. This is scoped as a one-time project, delivered over approximately 8–10 weeks.

Initiative 1: Accounts Payable Automation via Plooto
• Full setup and integration of Plooto with QBO
• Configure approval workflows so all payables are routed to the ED for one-click approval - no direct bank access required
• Set up bi-monthly AP payment aligned to bookkeeping cadence
• Replace the current manual OneDrive-based expense reimbursement tracking with a Plooto expense submission form
• Staff onboarding and support through the first 2 payment cycles

Initiative 2: Payroll Migration - ADP to QBO Payroll
• Migrate all 19 employees from ADP to QuickBooks Online Payroll
• Transfer YTD payroll balance, employee record, deductions
• Set up benefits deductions: medical, dental, LTD, AD&D in QBO
• Configure direct integration between QBO Payroll and ledger
• Parallel run for one pay cycle to validate accuracy before cutoff
• Staff training and documentation

Initiative 3: Invoicing & AR Automation
• Assess current invoicing setup and identify feasible tools
• Build standardized invoice templates for each service program
• Set up recurring monthly invoices where applicable
• Configure pre-authorized debit (PAD) or automated payment collection where families consent
• Set up automated invoice and payment reminder emails
• Establish a clear AR follow-up workflow for outstanding balances

PART C - YEAR-END AUDIT SUPPORT (ANNUAL ENGAGEMENT)
Year-end and audit support for the 2025–2026 fiscal year is scoped as a standalone one-time engagement, independent of the ongoing monthly retainer, and includes a full review of the year's books, outstanding reconciliations, and audit preparation.

Step 1: Year-End Book Review & Clean-Up
• Conduct a deep review of the full fiscal year (April–March)
• Identify and resolve any adjustments, reclassifications, accruals, or outstanding reconciling items
• Ensure all revenue streams (fees, grants, donations) are properly recorded and coded by program class
• Validate deferred revenue, prepaid expenses, and any balance sheet items requiring adjustment
• Reconcile ADP payroll records to QBO for the full fiscal year

Step 2: Audit Preparation & Working Papers
• Prepare year-end financial statements and all audit schedules, reconciliations, and supporting documentation
• Build the PBC (Prepared By Client) list and ensure items are complete before the auditor starts
• Coordinate year-end documents from the ED: board minutes, grant agreements, signed contracts

Step 3: Auditor Liaison & Audit Management
• Serve as the primary point of contact with the auditor
• Respond to auditor queries and information requests in 2 days
• Attend auditor meetings and manage all follow-up items
• Implement any post-audit adjustments and journal entries recommended by the auditor

PROPOSED FEES

PART A - MONTHLY ONGOING RETAINER
Service Module | Fee (per month)
• 1. Bookkeeping & Reconciliations: $1,250
• 2. Payroll Administration & Compliance: $1,000
• 3. Financial Reporting & Year End Compliance: (included)
TOTAL: $2,250 / month

PART B - PROCESS & DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION (ONE-TIME)
Service Module | Fee (one-time)
• 1. Accounts Payable Automation via Plooto: $2,000
• 2. Payroll Migration — ADP to QBO Payroll: $3,500
• 3. Invoicing & AR Automation: $1,800
TOTAL: $7,300 (one-time)

PART C - AUDIT SUPPORT (ANNUAL)
Service Module | Fee (annual)
• Year end audit support including reasonable clean up, audit prep and liaison with auditors*: $3,500
TOTAL: $3,500 (annual)

*Based on our initial review, some clean-up and reconciliation work will be required. Final fee will be confirmed once we have completed a full assessment of the books.
Note: Each initiative can be phased and contracted independently, allowing TACT to prioritize and implement changes at a pace that works for the organization.
Note: Does not include software subscription fees (QBO, Plooto, etc).

WHY US?
Sympl Solutions is committed to ensuring a high standard of financial clarity and timely support. We bring:
• A responsive, detail-oriented team
• Decade-long expertise in nonprofit and charity finance
• Streamlined tech integration and clear process flows
• BIPOC and immigrant-led leadership with lived experiences in community, social service and arts & culture
We value thoughtful system design, clarity in reporting, and building long-term trusted partnerships.
Any new requirements or adjustments can be discussed and integrated as needed. We work with transparency, flexibility, and a commitment to helping our partners thrive.
